principles: Document intent must be frozen before implementation.
Command existence is not enough; document DoD must be covered by evidence.
Control-plane reporting must not replace authoritative lifecycle gates.
Proof admissibility enforcement must not overclaim production authority.
Queue governance must preserve experiment evidence.
drivers: High-risk gate and proof-consumption code can block normal development if enforced too broadly.
The two execution-plan documents contain partial/future status that must be separated from delivered commitments.
B-5082 ProofStory gates are now enforce-mode and should be used to validate this story before DEV and DONE.

options.name: A: Parent ledger with staged implementation slices
pros: Preserves the full seven-milestone user intent ledger
Lets ProofStory gates detect missing coverage before DEV and DONE
Allows child stories if any milestone exceeds safe story size
cons: Requires more PLAN evidence before code work starts
May split implementation into follow-up child stories

options.name: B: Single monolithic implementation story
pros: Potentially faster if the gaps are small
cons: Repeats the earlier risk of marking document milestones done while only partially implemented
Harder to review runtime, queue, and proof enforcement independently

options.name: C: Audit-only story with no implementation
pros: Useful if all gaps are intentionally future work
cons: Does not close the user-requested missing capability gaps
Would not validate B-5082 through real DEV/REVIEW/DONE gates

chosen: A: Parent ledger with staged implementation slices
rationale: Choose the parent ledger with staged implementation slices because it best tests the B-5082 anti-shrinkage gates while still keeping high-risk enforcement work reviewable and reversible.

preMortem.scenario: The story declares DONE after making commands exist but not matching document DoD.
preMortem.trigger: Checklist items are treated as implementation tasks instead of milestone coverage claims.
preMortem.mitigation: Require milestone ledger, intent coverage, ProofStory contract, and DONE intent equivalence before closure.

preMortem.scenario: Runtime or proof enforcement breaks normal stories.
preMortem.trigger: Hard-block logic is enabled before warn-mode evidence and rollback configuration exist.
preMortem.consequence: Developers cannot advance unrelated stories or diagnose failures.
preMortem.mitigation: Stage enforcement with explicit config, warn-mode diagnostics, rollback notes, and focused smoke tests.

preMortem.scenario: Tier-C experiment stories are deleted or hidden as ordinary duplicates.
preMortem.trigger: Queue governance treats repeated experiment titles as cleanup targets without exception membership.
preMortem.consequence: Experiment evidence is lost or operators lose trust in the dashboard.
preMortem.mitigation: Register durable experiment-batch exceptions and keep malformed records visible as cleanup-required.

preMortem.scenario: Local proof evidence is over-read as production authority.
preMortem.trigger: Proof admissibility rollout confuses local gate evidence or handoff diagnostics with productionDone.
preMortem.consequence: The system makes a stronger claim than its proof boundary supports.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep productionDone false in local CLI core and assert the boundary in tests and docs.
